newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Lights out on Mir as crew battles new power snag.
newsitem.headline: Lights out on Mir as crew battles new power snag.

text.p: Russian Mission Control ordered the crew of the crippled Mir space station to shut down all unnecessary systems on Thursday, plunging it into darkness as engineers scrambled to sort out a new navigational problem.

"Close down all unnecessary systems," a Mission Control official told the crew. Officials told Reuters there was no light aboard and the power supply was at the minumum needed to keep Mir going following an unexplained malfunction in the system that keeps its solar batteries lined up on the Sun.
Valery Lyndin, a spokesman for Mission Control outside Moscow, told Reuters: "There was a drop in the power supply... It has fallen to the minimum level needed to run the ship."
"There is no threat to the crew," Lyndin added.
But tension rose palpably at Mission Control as experts crowded round terminals during a brief few minutes of radio contact with the two Russians and American aboard.

Mir lost up to half its electric power after a collision on June 25. The cosmonauts are due to attempt repairs next week. But meanwhile Mir has suffered repeated failures in the gyroscopic system that keeps its remaining solar panels lined up on the Sun. The problem has been countered by firing rocket motors.
